title: Humanistic Theories (Maslow, Rogers)
summary: Humanistic psychology: Maslow's hierarchy of needs and self-actualisation; Rogers' person-centred theory (self-concept, ideal self, congruence, unconditional positive regard).
objectives: Describe Maslow's five-level hierarchy of needs.
Describe Rogers' self-concept, congruence and unconditional positive regard.
revision: Humanistic theories: Maslow's hierarchy of needs (physiological → self-actualisation) and Rogers' person-centred theory (self-concept, congruence, unconditional positive regard).
traps: Maslow: physiological → safety → love/belonging → esteem → self-actualisation.
Rogers: self-concept + congruence + unconditional positive regard → growth.

i: Safety: security, stability, freedom from fear
Love and belonging: relationships, affection, family

notes.t: Needs are hierarchical: lower-level (deficiency) needs must be substantially satisfied before growth needs motivate behaviour.
The drive to realise one's full potential and become the best version of oneself.
The organised set of perceptions and beliefs about oneself.
Alignment between self-concept and experience; incongruence produces anxiety and defensiveness.
Accepting and valuing a person without conditions of worth, fostering growth.
Rogers emphasised the actualising tendency and the therapeutic conditions (genuineness, empathy, unconditional positive regard) that enable growth.
UGC NET frequently asks about Maslow's hierarchy order, self-actualisation, and Rogers' congruence and unconditional positive regard.

mnemonics.title: MR-SC
mnemonics.text: M — Maslow (hierarchy, self-actualisation), R — Rogers (self-concept, congruence, UPR), S — self-actualisation, C — congruence

flashcards.a: Accepting a person without conditions of worth.
